# Grafana dependency maintenance candidate

This candidate keeps Grafana 13.2.4, its original source/archive/tag, all thirteen complete official plugin packages, the eight maintained backend source revisions, existing backend-signature verification, frontend resources, runtime base and UID 472. It upgrades `github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4` to `v4.1.6` in the main module and `golang.org/x/net` to `v0.62.0` in the main and eight backend modules, together with the minimum `golang.org/x/*` versions declared by the fixed publisher modules. Security run 40673669969 at commit `ee370ae7841f7ae7cb85f7705d07dfb7ddd20d5e` completed the actual candidate compilation, nine full production graph captures, native ELF collection and complete raw Trivy/Syft/Grype scans. This successful material-collection job does not grant a vulnerability disposition or runtime approval.

The original `Dockerfile.grafana`, vendor locks, fixed OCI archive, human authorization and evidence bindings stay unchanged. The new recipe overlays the dependency locks in this directory on the original authenticated sources. It does not edit package version metadata, disable VCS information, filter findings, weaken signature checks, or inherit prior artifact decisions.

For a future separate candidate, build from the repository root (this produces new bytes requiring new review):

```sh
docker build -f deployment/docker/Dockerfile.grafana-security -t deepresearch-grafana-candidate:20261028 .
```

`source.lock.json` records the actual lock hashes and original source identities. The exact OCI archive SHA256 `849d3d86c9d51c6bda4c78d3091f7d457ba93dbd37e66aefcc87ef57b25cda70` received explicit human authorization on 2026-10-28, bound to request `7ab4c179c5224a4c7acde032640f71b84422120d92ae82ad251c506d37e8381d` and 28 individually reviewed target/advisory rows, expiring 2026-11-25. The pinned review records, genuine decision and verified transport are in `deployment/security/grafana-candidate-*.json`. The existing three native BusyBox MEDIUM records remain visible with the full raw scans. Every rebuilt or changed artifact requires a new review and authorization. Local daily services have not been started by this maintenance.

Primary references: [Go JOSE RSA JWK advisory](https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q), [Go html parser advisory](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6860), [Go html renderer advisory](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6866).

When built, the candidate recipe exports lossless full `go list -deps -json -mod=readonly` graphs, graph receipts, actual build-time locks and `go version -m` results under `/usr/share/deepresearch/grafana-candidate/`. These are build materials for independent review, not dispositions or approval. The collector preserves the full Go JSON, checks command completion and package errors, and records both raw and gzip SHA-256.

The five official backend packages that are not maintained in the eight-source rebuild set remain complete and unchanged: `elasticsearch`, `stackdriver`, `tempo`, `prometheus` and `zipkin`. Their existing `x/net` UNKNOWN findings may still require exact production-build applicability review. This candidate must not be described as a zero-finding image.

The original candidate artifact is 1,070,533,296 bytes, exceeding the connected artifact reader's 512 MiB download limit. The workflow may transport that exact ancestor archive only when every compile input remains byte-identical, after verifying the full ZIP digest and inner OCI digest. It then performs fresh complete scans and exports the OCI in hashed 64 MiB parts, four per upload group, with a complete reassembly manifest. Report artifacts are separate. Reuse preserves the original build commit; it never upgrades provenance or approval. `official-profiles.lock.json` and `capture_official_profiles.py` separately collect the remaining three official source profiles and compare their complete production dependency graphs with the actual native build information. Consistency alone is not a CVE decision.

`build_candidate_backends.py` imports `candidate_build_backends.py`, a small, auditable copy of the frozen backend builder. The original helper stays byte-for-byte unchanged. The copy still requires the source archive h1 and actual pinned Git revision; a present proxy `Origin` must match. When an authentic proxy omits `Origin`, it records that absence without inventing metadata and relies on the same archive checksum plus actual Git fetch/reset/revision checks. Actual source verification receipts are exported alongside the graphs. Immediately before each compile it runs `go mod download` with the default `sum.golang.org`, requires the `go.mod` SHA-256 to stay identical, and records the before/after `go.sum` hashes. The main stage applies the same guard before testing/building. All compilations still use `-mod=readonly`. Declared input `go.sum` hashes in `source.lock.json` are **not** claims about the final build-time sums; the image exports the actual locks and checksum-preparation receipts for independent review. No lock resolution result itself approves an artifact.

The approved archive is published as release `artifact-grafana-exact28-20261028` (ID `426729499`) in thirteen hashed 64 MiB parts. `python scripts/fetch_grafana_candidate.py` verifies the current authorization, pinned transport, live published release, all remote part digests, full OCI graph and fourteen actual ELF identities before loading `deepresearch-approved-grafana:20261028`. Compose and CI select that fixed image without rebuilding. Fresh complete Trivy/Syft/Grype reports feed `check_grafana_candidate_exact28.py`; unknown, new, missing, duplicate or changed blocking rows and all secret findings fail. The temporary candidate-build and official-source collection jobs have finished; the publication workflow is manual.
